english: A $3\times3$ matrix $A$ is transformed into the $3\times3$ identity matrix $I$ by the following elementary row operations, applied in the given order:
Then the sum of all the entries of $A$ is ______.
hindi: एक $3\times3$ आव्यूह $A$ को निम्नलिखित प्रारम्भिक पंक्ति संक्रियाएँ, दिए गए क्रम में, लगाने पर $3\times3$ तत्समक आव्यूह $I$ प्राप्त होता है:
तब $A$ की सभी प्रविष्टियों का योग ______ है।
solution: Each operation is left multiplication by an elementary matrix: $E_5E_4E_3E_2E_1A=I$, so $A^{-1}=E_5\cdots E_1$ and $A=E_1^{-1}E_2^{-1}E_3^{-1}E_4^{-1}E_5^{-1}$
So $A$ is obtained from $I$ by the inverse operations in reverse order: $R_3\to R_3-2R_2$, $R_2\to R_2-2R_1$, $R_3\to\frac12R_3$, $R_1\to R_1+2R_3$, $R_1\leftrightarrow R_2$
solution_full: Each elementary row operation equals left multiplication by the matrix $E$ obtained by doing that operation on $I$. Let $E_1,\ldots,E_5$ correspond to (i)-(v). Then $E_5E_4E_3E_2E_1A=I$.

Hence $A$ is invertible with $A^{-1}=E_5E_4E_3E_2E_1$ (the same operations applied to $I$ give $A^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}0&1&-2\\1&2&-4\\2&4&-6\end{pmatrix}$), and $A=\left(A^{-1}\right)^{-1}=E_1^{-1}E_2^{-1}E_3^{-1}E_4^{-1}E_5^{-1}$.

The inverse of each elementary operation is elementary: (i) is undone by $R_1\leftrightarrow R_2$, (ii) by $R_1\to R_1+2R_3$, (iii) by $R_3\to\frac12R_3$, (iv) by $R_2\to R_2-2R_1$, (v) by $R_3\to R_3-2R_2$.
$A=E_1^{-1}E_2^{-1}E_3^{-1}E_4^{-1}E_5^{-1}I$ means: starting from $I$, apply $E_5^{-1}$ first and $E_1^{-1}$ last.

Check: applying (i)-(v) to this $A$ gives $\begin{pmatrix}1&-2&1\\-2&1&0\\0&-1&\frac12\end{pmatrix}\to\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\-2&1&0\\0&-1&\frac12\end{pmatrix}\to\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\-2&1&0\\0&-2&1\end{pmatrix}\to\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&-2&1\end{pmatrix}\to I$.
originality_note: New: the matrix is not given; only the Gauss-Jordan sequence that reduces it to I is given, and A must be rebuilt by inverting the elementary operations in reverse order (way 5). Closest known: finding A^{-1} by applying row operations to [A | I]. Different because: the direction is reversed, so the student must use (E5...E1)^{-1} = E1^{-1}...E5^{-1} and the order of the inverse operations matters.

concept_use.Inverse of a square matrix: E5E4E3E2E1 A = I gives A^{-1} = E5...E1 and A = (A^{-1})^{-1} = E1^{-1}...E5^{-1}, using the inverse of a product in reverse order.
concept_use.Finding inverse by elementary operations: The row operations that reduce A to I are the Gauss-Jordan operations; undoing them in reverse order on I rebuilds A.

stem_review: Read as a student: every matrix and symbol is defined before use, every condition is stated, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed with sympy and is unique and equal to the Answer Plan; no hyperbolic functions or asymptotes. Checked: sympy applies (i)-(v) to the reconstructed A and obtains I; A^{-1} equals the operations applied to I; the sum of entries is -3/2 (a negative decimal as planned). The phrase 'applied in the given order' fixes the reading. Changed: No change.
key_step: Seeing that A = E1^{-1}...E5^{-1}, i.e. undoing the operations in reverse order on I.
justification: Two linked ideas (row operations as elementary matrices; inverse of a product in reverse order) with a precision risk in the order of operations and no options. Well above the row-equivalence check of 2026-P1-Q3 (L1); comparable to the matrix identity work of 2021-P1-Q14 (L3).
